q: Why do the comb areas at the ends of a moving walk need special safety attention?
o: Moving pallets meet the fixed floor there, where shoes and fingers can be trapped
They carry the full weight of the passengers on the walk
They hold the drive motor that moves the pallets
They are where the handrail speed is set
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: The comb teeth mesh with the pallet grooves to lift feet and objects off the moving surface. A switch stops the walk if something jams the comb.

q: Why must access to elevator and escalator machinery be planned in the design?
o: Codes require the machinery to be visible to passengers
The equipment must be inspected, repaired and replaced safely
Access space is needed only while the unit is installed
Access space is needed only to meet ventilation rules
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Motors, controllers and brakes are serviced for the life of the building. Machine spaces, pits and escalator wells need safe, lit access routes.

q: What is the elevator governor for?
o: Controlling how fast the doors open
Levelling the car with each floor
Detecting overspeed and tripping the safety gear
Balancing the car against the counterweight
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: The governor is a rope-driven sheave that turns with the car. If the car goes too fast, it first cuts power, then grips its rope, which pulls the safety gear onto the rails.

q: What does the comb plate at an escalator landing do?
o: It holds the handrail where it turns at the newel end
It covers the pit that houses the drive machinery
It stops the steps if the handrail breaks
Its teeth mesh with the step grooves to guide feet and objects off the steps
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: The comb plate is the step-to-floor transition. It is fitted with a switch that stops the escalator if something is caught.

o: In the pit, below the car and the counterweight
In the machine room, beside the brake
On top of the car, above the crosshead
In the lobby, behind the hall call buttons
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Buffers are springs or oil cylinders that stop a car or counterweight that runs past the lowest landing.

q: Which escalator area is a known entrapment point for soft shoes and loose clothing?
o: The top of the moving handrail
The gap between the moving steps and the skirt panel
The middle of a step tread
The glass balustrade panel
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: The steps slide past the fixed skirt panel with only a few millimetres of gap. Skirt deflector brushes and safety switches are fitted there.

q: What does the brake on a traction machine do?
o: Levels the car with the floor before the doors open
Grips the guide rails when the car overspeeds
Stops the drive and holds the car still at a floor
Absorbs the impact at the bottom of the pit
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: The machine brake is spring-applied and held open electrically, so it sets whenever power is lost. Gripping the rails is the job of the safety gear.

q: Why must elevator shafts be enclosed in fire-rated construction?
o: The rating keeps the car cool in normal service
The rating reduces noise from the machine room
The enclosure carries the weight of the car
Shafts link the floors and would otherwise carry smoke and fire upward
ref: NBC Rule VII; Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: A shaft is a vertical opening through every floor. Fire-rated walls and self-closing doors keep it from acting as a chimney.

q: Why are ordinary passenger elevators recalled and not used for evacuation in a fire?
o: Shafts can fill with smoke and power may fail, trapping people
Elevators move too slowly to help at all
Elevator doors lock shut for good when an alarm sounds
The counterweight is released during a fire
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Heat-sensitive buttons can call cars to the fire floor, and smoke enters shafts. Cars are recalled and kept for firefighters unless designed for occupant evacuation.

q: Why is an escalator fitted with emergency stop buttons?
o: So it can slow down when traffic is light
So it can be stopped quickly if someone falls or is caught
So it can reverse direction at rush hour
So it can be shut off at closing time only
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: The stop switches are at each landing. They stop the steps under control, not so abruptly that riders fall.

q: What does a door interlock do?
o: Reopens the door when a passenger is in the way
Holds the doors open during fire-service operation
Keeps the car from moving unless the hoistway door is closed and locked
Levels the car before the doors open
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Each hoistway door has an interlock. It locks the door shut unless the car is at that floor and breaks the safety circuit if a door is open.

q: What does the safety gear of an elevator do?
o: Absorbs the energy of the car at the bottom of the pit
Detects overspeed and signals the controller
Holds the drive sheave when the car is parked
Grips the guide rails to stop the car when it overspeeds
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: The safety gear is mounted under the car. When the governor trips it, wedges clamp onto the rails and bring the car to a stop.

q: Where is an escalator's emergency stop button usually placed?
o: At the top and bottom landings, on the newel or skirt
Only in the machine space under the landing
Only in the building's fire control room
In the middle of the handrail
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Stop buttons must be where a bystander can reach them fast, at each end of the escalator, and on long units also along the run.

q: In Phase I fire-service recall, what do the elevators do when smoke is detected?
o: Stop at the nearest floor and let passengers out
Return nonstop to the designated recall floor and park with doors open
Keep running normally until the power is cut
Rise to the top floor and lock their doors
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Recall brings all cars to the main floor, or an alternate floor if the fire is there, so firefighters can take control under Phase II.
